isolation.evidence: Session permissions specify read-only filesystem access and approval_policy=never. Reading .review-permission-probe returned source-write-probe. Attempting printf x >> .review-permission-probe exited 1: operation not permitted. Launcher also supplied successful read/denied-write verification. Final git status contained only the preexisting untracked probe.

scope: Independent inspection of approved PTO sprint acceptance, target revision, application/domain code, browser/component/unit tests, preview hosting, CI and review launcher. acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Anonymous user receives a correct explained result or actionable no-results without credentials/network/auth.
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: Static implementation has no authentication or network dependency in calculation. Independent in-memory domain probes passed, but the actual welcome-to-result browser journey could not execute.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Allowance/balance, workweek, confirmed holidays, duration, periods and blackouts affect results consistently.
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: Inspected validation and bounded enumeration in src/domain/pto/index.ts. Independent assertions verified holiday cost, zero balance, zero-PTO weekends and inclusive blackout rejection. Workweek is explicitly restricted to Monday–Friday.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: PTO dates, holiday contribution and remaining balance reconcile; unconfirmed holidays do not reduce PTO.
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: Domain code subtracts only explicitly supplied employer holidays on scheduled workdays and deduplicates holiday dates. Independent Thanksgiving probe returned four PTO days; cross-year probe returned remaining balances 2026=0 and 2027=1.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Zero balance permits zero-PTO breaks and insufficient balance never yields falsely feasible options.
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: Independent assertions passed for a zero-balance weekend and rejection of a nine-day window requiring PTO.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Invalid inputs are rejected and editing/recalculation updates results.
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: Malformed-date domain assertion passed and edited() clears stale results in source. UI validation recovery and recalculation could not be independently executed.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Stable ranking, cross-year behavior and source assumptions are visible and tested; timezone cannot change calendar results.
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: Code sorts by PTO count then ISO start date and displays the ranking assumptions. Sixteen independent assertions passed across America/New_York, Pacific/Auckland and UTC, including cross-year remaining balances. Existing test source includes tie, leap-day and DST fixtures; its test runner was blocked.

findings.evidence: When Share.share rejects, the handler only displays 'You can copy the dates from your result.' There is no clipboard operation or selectable summary control. Reproduction: use a browser without navigator.share and press Share this idea. The inspected available react-native-web Share implementation rejects in that case. The approved plan specifies native share/web copy fallback; plain React Native Text results are not configured selectable, further weakening the suggested manual fallback.
missingTests: Browser without navigator.share copies a complete privacy-safe summary.
Sharing rejection provides a usable recovery control.
Share payload excludes allowance, balance, blackouts and holiday names.

findings.evidence: Cross-year balances initialize to 20/10 and calculate() automatically submits them when start/end years differ. A user can enter only a current-year balance, extend the range into January and receive a feasible next-year recommendation without explicitly supplying next-year balances. This conflicts with the approved requirement that cross-year windows require explicit balances for both years and risks presenting assumed future leave as available.
missingTests: Cross-year search requires explicit next-year allowance and balance before calculation.
Changing the search years cannot silently reuse balances associated with different years.
